requirements.native_behavior: Native SQL replication checks the expected source error and statement outcome. A source error does not always mean that no object changed.
requirements.current_behavior: Query events with a nonzero source error stop apply before target SQL. Partial source DDL results are not reproduced.
requirements.acceptance: Define and journal object-specific partial results before implementing replay. Do not blindly retry the complete statement.

requirements.source_behavior: Active executable comments remain in logged Query SQL. Native source parsing changes inactive version comments into ordinary comments before logging.
requirements.native_behavior: The target evaluates executable comments against its own exact server version. A lower target can acknowledge a fully inactive statement without a schema change. Five/six-digit parsing follows the target version.
requirements.current_behavior: Original executable comments are sent to MySQL. A separate byte-preserving parser view predicts metadata under the target version gate. Fully inactive DDL has a durable no-op intent and advances only after target acknowledgement. Existing compatibility rules and object/filter policies apply to active clauses. requirements.acceptance: Retain native gate behavior, original and target SQL, journal outcomes and exact schema checks across restart and replay. Qualify remaining lexical and failure combinations without claiming complete MySQL grammar support.
